title: Harun al-Rashid and the Three Poets
logline: A handmaid's witty excuse, 'day erases the promise of night', becomes the caliph's poetry contest; Abu Nuwas imagines the night so exactly that he is nearly beheaded as a spy, then talks his way to a double prize.
moral: Imagination is not evidence: a poet can describe what he never saw, and a fair ruler listens before he punishes.
tone: Light court comedy with one sharp scare. Discreet and playful about the night scene; the threat is real for ten seconds and then melts into relief and a money gag.

beats.summary: The caliph cannot sleep and walks his palace at night.
He finds the handmaid he favours, tipsy, and asks to stay.
She promises: come tomorrow night. The moon-knot promise balloon is born.
Next day her answer arrives: day erases the promise of night. The sun rubs out the moon.
Stung and amused, Harun summons three poets and sets the line as their theme.
Al-Raqashi: a sleepless lover betrayed at dawn. Competent, safe.
Abu Musab: a heart on fire, overacted.
Abu Nuwas's poem replays the real night, down to the slipped shawl.
Too close: the poem and Harun's memory are the same picture.
Ten thousand each for the two safe poets; Abu Nuwas holds out empty hands.
You were watching us! The order to behead him; the guard steps in.
I never left my house. You gave the theme; a poet imagines what he has not seen.
Harun calms and sees that a poem is no proof of spying.
Pardon and twenty thousand dirhams: double the others.
DOUBLE: the rivals stare at their single purses.

subtitles.ar: لم يستطع الخليفة هارون الرشيد النوم في إحدى الليالي،|فخرج يتمشى في قصره.|رأى جارية يحبها وقد شربت الخمر،|فاقترب منها وطلب أن يقضي معها بقية الليل.
subtitles.en: One sleepless night Harun al-Rashid|walked through his palace.|He saw an enslaved handmaid he favored, affected by wine,|and asked to spend the night with her.

subtitles.ar: قالت الجارية: لم أكن أتوقع زيارتك؛|تعال غدًا ليلًا. تركها الخليفة على وعدها.|وعندما أرسل إليها في اليوم التالي،|جاء جوابها: وعد الليل يمحوه النهار.
subtitles.en: She said she was not prepared|and asked him to come the following night.|The next day, when he sent for her,|she answered, “Day erases the promise of night.”

subtitles.ar: أدهشت العبارة هارون وأغضبته قليلًا،|فدعا ثلاثة شعراء في مجلسه.|قال لهم: أريد شعرًا يدخل فيه هذا المعنى:|وعد الليل يمحوه النهار. تقدم الشاعر الرقاشي أولًا.
subtitles.en: The reply astonished and annoyed Harun.|He called three poets|and ordered each to compose verses|around the line about a nighttime promise erased by day.

subtitles.ar: أنشد الرقاشي أبياتًا عن عاشق لا ينام من الحزن،|وعن امرأة غيرت وعدها عند الصباح.|ثم تقدم أبو مصعب، فوصف قلبًا مشتعلًا بالشوق،|وكرر عبارة الجارية بأسلوب آخر.
subtitles.en: Al-Rakashi recited the grief of a sleepless lover|betrayed at dawn.|Abu Musab followed, describing another heart burning with longing|and repeating her words.

subtitles.ar: أما أبو نواس فقال شعرًا يصف ليلة داخل القصر،|وجارية شربت الخمر، وثوبها الذي انزاح،|ووعدها الذي تغير عند طلوع الشمس.|كان وصفه قريبًا جدًا مما حدث فعلًا.
subtitles.en: Abu Nuwas instead described a night in the palace:|a handmaid drinking wine, displaced clothing,|and a promise withdrawn with sunrise.|His verses closely matched the event.

subtitles.ar: أمر هارون أن يعطى الرقاشي وأبو مصعب|عشرة آلاف درهم لكل منهما.|ثم التفت غاضبًا إلى أبي نواس وقال:|لقد كنت تراقبنا البارحة! وأمر بقطع رأسه.
subtitles.en: Harun awarded the first two poets|ten thousand dirhams each.|Then, accusing Abu Nuwas of secretly watching the encounter,|he ordered his execution.

subtitles.ar: صاح أبو نواس: والله ما خرجت من بيتي تلك الليلة!|أنت أعطيتني موضوع القصيدة،|والشاعر يتخيل ما لم يره.|ثم ذكر للخليفة أن الشعراء قد يقولون ما لا يفعلون.
subtitles.en: Abu Nuwas protested that he had stayed home.|The caliph had supplied the theme, he argued,|and poets imagine things they never witness;|he quoted scripture on poets’ inventions.

subtitles.ar: هدأ هارون حين سمع الجواب،|وأدرك أن الشعر ليس دليلًا على التجسس.|عفا عن أبي نواس، ثم منحه عشرين ألف درهم،|أي ضعف مكافأة كل واحد من الشاعرين الآخرين.
subtitles.en: Harun accepted that a poem|was no proof of spying,|pardoned Abu Nuwas, and awarded him twenty thousand|dirhams—twice either other poet’s prize.

new_assets.name: person costume presets (poet)
new_assets.description: The planned 'poet' preset (AN-103) on the person costume layer: robe, sash, small tilted white turban with a hanging tail, short pointed beard, quill in the turban (quill: false for the others). Three poets by pal and age: Abu Nuwas green/young (default), Al-Raqashi brown/age 0.7, Abu Musab blue and 8 % wider.
new_assets.implementation: Add a COSTUME entry in Library/cast/people.js copying 'merchant' with a smaller turban (rotate the headwear path 0.15 rad), tail as a 3-point shape, quill as a thin white triangle with a black nib; width via an optional pal/option 'wide: 1.08' scaling the torso x. Opt-in, so regression stays identical.

new_assets.name: person costume presets (guard, executioner)
new_assets.description: The planned guard preset: pointed helmet with neck cloth, short tunic, sash, moustache, default lid 0.4. Used for one palace guard who stands in for the executioner; hold:'sword' rests the planned sword on the shoulder.
new_assets.implementation: COSTUME entry: helmet = half ellipse + spike triangle + neck cloth rectangle; tunic to the knees; sword drawn by the scene at the hand point from P.hands, rotated to lie on the shoulder.

new_assets.name: person shawl (shoulder slip)
new_assets.description: Opt-in field shawl 0..1 on the lady / maiden / villageWoman presets: a short shoulder shawl over the robe (yellow with red dots). 0 = sits evenly on both shoulders; 1 = slid off the near shoulder and hanging at the elbow, showing only the sleeve of the robe underneath. The discreet stand-in for the script's displaced garment; the robe itself never changes.
new_assets.implementation: Two shape() polygons over the torso: a band across both shoulders (about 150 wide, 34 deep at s 1) whose left end point is lerped from the shoulder (x -38, y -150) down to the elbow (x -52, y -100) by the field; dotPat fill. Drawn only when shawl is defined.

new_assets.name: iconBalloon
new_assets.description: The planned wordless picture balloon (single and strip modes). This film's icons: moonKnot (yellow moon disc r 46 with a small red knotted ribbon under it = the promise), sun (disc r 40 with 10 rays, slides across and erases the moon: moon alpha to 0.15 dotted outline, three crumbs), cushion-for-two, keyhole with a peeping eye (eye has gaze), scroll, scimitar (planned icon), tiny talking poets, struck (red X). Also shrinks to a 90 px THEME badge parked top right in panel space.
new_assets.implementation: Balloon body = HP speech-box primitive (S.box) with a tail polygon; icons are small functions (ell() discs, shape() rays, eyeAt() for the keyhole eye); eraseP 0..1 drives the sun x and the moon alpha; scale and position keyed with kfn so the same drawing serves balloon and badge.

new_assets.name: verseRibbon
new_assets.description: The planned poetry ribbon (AN-103): a paper band 44 wide with squiggle lines that unrolls from the speaker along a curve (open 0..1) and rolls up again; shows recitation without lettering.
new_assets.implementation: Sample a bezier into 24 points up to open; offset the points by the normal to make a strip polygon; squiggles as short sine strokes at every third sample; a small spiral at the leading end.

new_assets.name: wineCup
new_assets.description: Planned small stemmed cup with tilt, glint and empty options.
new_assets.implementation: Trapezoid bowl, stem line, ellipse foot; fill as a clipped red band; rotate about the stem base by tilt.

new_assets.name: purse
new_assets.description: Planned fat coin purse with a drawstring and a coin mark.
new_assets.implementation: ell() body with dot shading, gathered neck as three small triangles, string as two strokes; swing() for the lag when carried.

new_assets.name: spear, sword
new_assets.description: Planned sword as a scimitar, carried only.
new_assets.implementation: Curved blade as a 6-point shape with a white fill and one glint line, yellow cross guard and grip.

new_assets.name: handOver
new_assets.description: Planned helper: a small object passes from one hand to another in 0.25 s with a weight dip on arrival; both gazes follow it. Used for the four purses.
new_assets.implementation: Object position = lerp(handA world point, handB world point, ease(t)); receiver hand target dips 8 units on a damped spring (rebound).

new_assets.name: palaceHall (night option)
new_assets.description: Night lighting for palaceHall as already planned by AN-092 and AN-103: moon and stars in the arches, lit lamps, navy wash. Most of it exists as options (wall 'blue', lampsLit, outside callback).
new_assets.implementation: Call palaceHall({wall:'blue', lampsLit:true, throne:false, dais:false, outside:(c) => skyCycle(c, 0.75)}) and add a navy rect at alpha 0.25 clipped to the floor, with lamp circles left clear.

owner_questions: SCRIPT: P3 Arabic ends with 'Al-Raqashi the poet stepped forward first' but the English translation has no such sentence; both are kept verbatim.

SCRIPT: P2 Arabic includes 'the caliph left her on her promise', which the English omits; P7 English says he 'quoted scripture' where the Arabic only says he reminded the caliph that poets may say what they do not do; both kept verbatim.
The wine is shown as a small cup, pink cheeks and one HIC! lettering (default: shown this lightly; alternative: no cup, only a sleepy sway).
The request to 'spend the night' is staged as a polite open-handed gesture and a picture balloon of a moon and a cushion for two, with no touching (default chosen).
The 'garment that slipped' is staged as a shoulder shawl sliding off one shoulder over a fully covering robe (default chosen), so the poem can match the real event without anything immodest.
The beheading order is softened: a guard with a sword on his shoulder steps in and a scimitar icon appears; the sword is never raised (default chosen).
The scripture reference in P7 is not quoted or shown as text; it is a plain picture balloon of poets talking versus doing (default chosen).

Invented lettering beyond the script: NIGHT, HIC!, TOMORROW NIGHT, HMPH!, name tags AL-RAQASHI / ABU MUSAB / ABU NUWAS, 1 / 3 to 3 / 3, THE SAME?!, 10,000, YOU SPIED!, GULP!, AT HOME!, PHEW!, 20,000, DOUBLE!, THE END (default: all kept; the name tags use the common spelling Al-Raqashi although the English subtitle says Al-Rakashi).
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template; set LIFE.t = t each frame for auto-blinks; override lid by hand where the plan gives one. Panel-only shake (template) for the single shake at 115.7.
One room, two lightings: build hallNight and hallDay from palaceHall with different options and bake each once. Use HALL anchors (door, dais, throne.sitY) rather than the approximate numbers here.

The moon-knot / sun-eraser picture is the film's motif: write it once as an iconBalloon icon with eraseP 0..1 and reuse it at 23.9, 34.9-37.0, 39.8 (badge), 52.1-54.3, 77.1, 92.3-94.1, 127.7 and 160.2.

The handmaid tableau (cushion, cup, hiccup, shawl slip) must be ONE function jariyaTableau(ctx, tLocal, opts) used live in S2, inside Abu Nuwas's cloud in S9 (thoughtCloud inside, scale 0.5) and in Harun's memory cloud in S10, so the match is exact by construction.

thoughtCloud is in Library/fx/fx.js: thoughtCloud(ctx, x, y, w, h, t, {p, tail, inside(c, t), scale, at}). Keep figures inside at least 110 px on screen; at camera zoom 1.3 a cloud scale of 0.45-0.5 does this.
Speaker on one side, listeners on the other: the reciter always stands at x 500 facing the throne; clouds go up and left over the waiting poets (cloud bottom edge above y 530, heads at about y 708).
Groups never move in unison: use stagger(i) for the three poets' reactions, bows and the sidestep at 101.4.
Sound: the narration has only two real pauses (80.28-81.22 and 101.32-102.16). Use exactly three quiet effects: pop 80.75, low thud 101.75, chime 160.0. Nothing else; SND master 0.6.
Subtitles come from the subtitles array (verbatim, 4 chunks per paragraph); time each chunk to its first word from timing.json.
Counters: S.counter for 10,000 and 20,000 (use a comma, no dashes). Name tags with S.label at 28 px or more (1280 x 720 scale), below the figure and clear of the caption panel.
warnings: Eight scenes need the planned iconBalloon; if it is not in Library yet, build it in this story first and move it later.
Five to six figures share the hall in S5, S11, S12, S14 and S16: keep them at s 0.75-0.8 and at least 110 units apart so name tags and counters do not collide.
Adult themes (wine, a night visit, a death sentence) are in the script; every staging choice here is deliberately discreet. See owner_questions.
No sound effects can be placed during almost all of the film (continuous narration); visual accents must carry the beats.
The clouds in S9-S10 carry the key reveal: check at phone size that the slipped shawl reads in the cloud (the shawl is yellow on red for contrast).
